claimedValue: All 26 R8 merge conflicts touched only Praxis .ros/ state files; no application-code conflicts occurred in this rehearsal
recomputedValue: PR-merge level: exactly 26 of 49 PR merge commits conflict on replay, the same 26 PRs the coordinator logged, every one only in .ros/context/current.json and/or .ros/events/events.jsonl (reproduced). Rehearsal level: 60 of 86 merge commits conflict on replay; 4 'merge origin/main into r8/<branch>' commits (branches of PRs #10, #12, #19, #36) conflicted in 6 non-state files: src/Causa.App/Program.fs, src/Causa.Persistence/Classify.fs, src/Causa.Persistence/GitHubRequests.fs, tests/Causa.TestSupport/StatefulFake.fs, tests/Causa.Invariants/Negative/INV22.fs, .github/workflows/live.yml. Git's own '# Conflicts:' trailers in those merge commit messages list the same 6 paths (51 merge commits carry such trailers).
method: Fresh scratch clone /home/user/sprint-scratch/V1/r8 of indy-init-rehearsal-008@fd8fba9; for every 2-parent merge commit `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only --no-messages P1 P2`, conflicted paths parsed; branch-side merges of a PR found as merge commits in P1..P2 of its PR merge commit; cross-checked with the '# Conflicts:' block git writes into merge messages and with `git show --cc` (non-empty combined diffs for Program.fs, INV22.fs, live.yml).
discrepancies: merges.jsonl records conflicts only at the PR-merge step. Application-code conflicts were resolved by the task agents when they merged main into their branches and never reached the log; PRs #12, #19 and #36 are logged as conflict:false although their branches had application/CI conflicts, and #10 is logged with only .ros/context/current.json.
11 PRs logged conflict:false had branch-side conflicts (mostly .ros).
notes: The statement '26 conflicts, all .ros' is true of the coordinator's PR merges only. The rehearsal-level inference ('no application-code conflicts occurred') is contradicted: at least 4 merges conflicted in application, test or CI code. The conflict rate depends on what counts as a merge: 26/49 PR merges (53%) vs 60/86 merge commits (70%). Resolution seconds were not re-verified (coordinator-logged).

claimedValue: R8 lane utilisation mean 2.15 of 6 (36%), peak 5; 350 one-minute samples 'T0 to merge freeze'; 34 minutes with none active
recomputedValue: Task-agent transcript spans, 350 samples from T0: mean 2.151, peak 5 concurrent agents, 35.9%, 41 zero minutes, 756.75 agent-minutes. But merge freeze is T+379 (23:50:28Z): over 379 samples mean 2.01 (33.6%), 63 zero minutes. Counting distinct lanes (roles) rather than agents: mean 2.11 (350) / 1.97 (379), peak 4. Using Praxis work start->finalize spans instead of transcript spans: mean 1.57 (26%), peak 4.

Transcript spans include pre-'work start' time (e.g. T18 agent span begins 10 min before its Praxis work start); Praxis spans give 1.57.
notes: Headline 2.15 / peak 5 reproduces under Track A's exact window and unit (agents). The metric is sensitive to window end, span source and agent-vs-lane counting; range 1.57-2.15 mean, 26-36%.

claimedValue: 67% of CI job-minutes in R2-R10 timed windows were in failed/cancelled/timed_out runs (10,458 of 15,568 ceil-minutes)
recomputedValue: Primary sample (100 runs per repo; census for R7, R9): 65.6% (bootstrap 95% CI 56.5%-71.9%); estimated 13,722 job-minutes (CI 11,225-16,401), 9,000 red (CI 6,409-11,661). Per repo: R2 22.0%, R3 19.4%, R4 46.5%, R5 39.8%, R6 81.2%, R7 58.7% (census), R8 30.0%, R9 28.0% (census), R10 89.2%; excluding R6 and R10 36.8%. Replicate sample (40 per repo, independent draw): 58.2% (CI 42.3%-70.1%).
method: Own read-only fetch of the Actions API (curl GET via session proxy): every run created in [T0, T0+420 min) listed with the server-side created filter; stratified simple random sample per repository (seed 20261108, conclusion != skipped); jobs fetched with filter=all (all attempts). Job-minutes = per-job ceil(minutes); a run is red if its conclusion is failure/cancelled/timed_out/startup_failure/action_required; expansion estimator per stratum, summed; 2,000-rep stratified bootstrap.
inputs: GitHub Actions API, fetched 2026-11-08 19:01-19:15Z (data/ci-sample-100/manifest.json, data/ci-sample/manifest.json, sampled run ids listed)
T0 per rehearsal read from each repo's own evidence (scripts/fetch_ci_sample.py WINDOWS)
discrepancies: Window: every T0 matches the rehearsal's documented start and the in-window run populations equal Track A's exactly (128/114/135/436/427/54/566/50/281 non-skipped). But the fixed T0+420 window does not match activity: R2 ran to its accepted release at T+721 min (87 runs in the 17 h after the window), R3's timed phase ended at T+127 (09:39Z) yet the window runs to T+420, R4 has 249 runs in the 17 h after the window, R3 had 35 preflight runs in the 2 h before T0, and R5's T0 is defined post hoc as its first green check.
Definition sensitivity (primary sample): 65.6% with ceil-minutes attributed by run conclusion; 76.4% with unrounded job seconds; 54.3% if only jobs that themselves failed/cancelled count.
notes: Claim reproduced within sampling error: 67% lies inside the CI and the census strata (R7 59%, R9 28%) match Track A's figures exactly. 'Red' includes cancellations of superseded runs (largely R6, R10) and successful jobs inside failed runs, so it is not a waste or defect measure on its own.

claimedValue: CI rebuilds the pinned Praxis verifier from source on every run: 688 job-minutes (8.4% of step time) across R2-R10
recomputedValue: Rebuild-from-source is confirmed: echelon-foundations.yml in R2-R6 and R8-R10 calls kemiller2002/praxis foundations-verify.yml (@aa7c7ca, R6 @398af6d), which checks out praxis at the pinned commit and runs `dotnet build` with no build cache; the step ran in 197/197 sampled foundations runs. Minutes are lower: post-stratified estimate 607 min (95% CI 580-632; replicate sample 618, CI 591-645), about 1 min per foundations run x 594 foundations runs, roughly 7.4-8.0% of step time (unstratified sample share 7.2%, CI 5.6%-9.2%).
method: Workflow YAML read in every rehearsal repo and in the pinned Praxis reusable workflow (read from a scratch clone); step durations of the step named 'Build pinned Praxis verifier' from V1's sample; post-stratified by workflow: population count of Echelon foundations runs per repo x mean verifier minutes per sampled foundations run; bootstrap CI.
inputs: indy-init-rehearsal-002..010 .github/workflows/*.yml at the revisions checked out
discrepancies: 688 is wrong for the verifier. Track A's own step data puts 604.0 min on 'Build pinned Praxis verifier'; the other 84.5 min is R5's 'Build the candidate and the plan verifier', which builds the application (App.slnx) and Indy-init's requirements compiler, not Praxis. The corrected figure is about 604-607 min, about 7.4% of step time.
'Every run' means every run of the Echelon foundations workflow (about 27% of in-window runs), not every CI run.
R6's workflow has a fingerprint cache gate that could skip the build, but the build was never skipped in the sample (inputs changed on every commit).
R7 has no foundations workflow; its praxis-autonomy.yml also builds Praxis from source (`dotnet build praxis/src/Praxis.Cli/...`, about 33 min, census) under a step name the claim does not count.
notes: The recommendation (cache or ship a prebuilt pinned verifier) still holds; the size is about 10 job-hours across the nine windows, not 11.5.

claimedValue: REL-001 run-02: every arm 39/39; optimized Echelon $0.1555 vs bare $0.1147 per correct requirement (+35.5%)
recomputedValue: 80 confirmatory non-U6 trials (20 per arm; pilot and U6 excluded per the preregistration): every arm 39/39 correct units; cost per correct requirement bare $0.1147 ($4.4743/39), directives $0.1390, original Echelon $0.1520, optimized Echelon $0.1555 ($6.0646/39); optimized vs bare +35.54%. Tokens per correct 221,834 vs 304,458.
method: Own pricing of each trial's token buckets (run02.tokens.byKind: input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite 5m/1h) with the price table; pooled ratio sum(cost)/sum(correct units) per arm. Correct units from each trial's oracle-scored run02.units. Experiment cost fields used only as a cross-check (max per-trial difference 4e-7 USD); analysis scripts not used.
notes: Partial: token buckets and oracle verdicts are the experiment's own per-trial records; raw transcripts and oracle re-runs were not available/re-executed. Definitional caveat: output tokens are a transcript lower bound in all 80 trials (about 22 tokens per request, streaming-start counts), so output is only 1.3-1.7% of computed cost. True cost per correct requirement is higher in every arm, and the +35.5% gap could move if true output differs between arms; the report discloses the lower bound (REPORT-run-02.md:237) but the headline does not. 39/39 in all arms is a ceiling: the experiment cannot show a quality difference.
